name: Centre de Processament de Dades IBM

profile.reading:
This is the building OpenStreetMap names Centre de Processament de Dades IBM, using the Catalan phrase for a data processing centre. Reverse geocoding the recorded position puts it on Carrer de Creu Casas i Sicart in the Centre Direccional at Bellaterra, in the municipality of Cerdanyola del Valles in the Valles Occidental county of Barcelona province, postcode 08193. That district is the planned science and technology quarter next to the Autonomous University of Barcelona and the ALBA synchrotron, which is a deliberate location for research and enterprise computing rather than an accident of industrial land.

IBM converted an existing site here into what it announced on 31 January 2013 as its first cloud data centre in Spain and, at that point, the ninth cloud centre in its global network, bringing it into service by the middle of that year. The infrastructure it was built on had already been serving Spanish financial sector clients before the cloud conversion, so the 2013 date marks a change of role for a working site rather than the construction of a new one.

The Catalan regional government became an early anchor customer. The Generalitat de Catalunya consolidated one of its own data processing centres into the facility, covering healthcare, welfare and family services systems, under a contract reported at roughly 140 million euros over ten years. That kind of public sector consolidation is the reason a site of this type carries weight out of proportion to its physical footprint, since a single building ends up holding the transactional systems for a regional health service.

This facility should not be confused with IBM's Client Center Barcelona, in the Eixample district of the city itself, which is a client briefing and demonstration space rather than a production data centre. The two are frequently conflated in listings that key on the IBM name and a Barcelona address.

The record here is thin on physical detail, and it is worth saying so plainly. IBM has not published an IT load, a utility power service rating, standby generator capacity, on-site generation, technical floor area or a current operational status for this building, and none is recorded here. Large enterprise technology companies routinely run client facing and internal processing sites that are never individually marketed the way commercial colocation providers document their halls, and this is one of them.

The OpenStreetMap provenance is straightforward. The footprint was first mapped in September 2015 by a contributor working on the area, was given its Centre de Processament de Dades IBM name in June 2016 by another mapper, and received its telecom data centre tag in August 2023 in a JOSM changeset explicitly hashtagged for a Barcelona data centre survey and sourced to metropolitan area and Catalan cartographic institute orthophotography. The name and the tag were added by different people at different times, and neither edit rests on an operator disclosure.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05. Two problems fixed. First, the prior public text described this registry own research process (could not pull a fresh primary source, sourcing available this session) which does not belong in reader-facing prose, and it is removed. Second, Wikipedia was dropped from sources per registry policy and the generic IBM corporate-description paragraph it supported was cut rather than re-asserted. Location tightened using Nominatim reverse geocode on the stored coordinates, which returns Carrer de Creu Casas i Sicart, Centre Direccional, Bellaterra, Cerdanyola del Valles, 08193, the planned science quarter beside the UAB campus and the ALBA synchrotron, a sharper placement than the previous Cerdanyola del Valles metro-area statement. OSM provenance added from the version history, v1 2015-09-01 by EliziR as an unnamed building, v2 2016-06-08 by Galifardeu adding the Catalan name, v3 2023-08-04 by jqngarcia adding telecom=data_center in changeset 139437346, comment "#DataCenters #Barcelona", created_by JOSM, source "Ortofoto AMB, Ortofoto 1.2500 iCGC". The 2013 IBM cloud conversion, ninth global cloud centre, mid-2013 service date and the Generalitat contract reported at about 140 million euros over ten years are retained from the Data Center Dynamics Spanish edition coverage. No capacity, area or power figure exists and none is asserted.
